question_en: When is the deadline to apply for a primary school place?
evidence: close on 15 January
reference_answer: Applications open in September and close on 15 January. You apply through your local council, a year before your child can start school.

question_en: What is the last date to apply for a secondary school place?
evidence: by 31 October
reference_answer: You must apply by 31 October. Applications usually open on 1 September.

question_en: When will I find out which primary school my child has been offered?
evidence: primary schools on 16 April
reference_answer: Councils send primary school offers on 16 April (the next working day if that is a weekend or bank holiday).

question_en: How long do I have to appeal if my child is refused a school place?
evidence: at least 20 school days
reference_answer: The admission authority must allow you at least 20 school days to appeal from when it sends the decision letter.

question_en: Can I be fined for taking my child on holiday during term time?
evidence: fined or face legal action for taking your child on holiday
reference_answer: Yes. You can be fined or face legal action. The council can fine each parent £80, rising to £160 if not paid within 21 days.

question_en: Can my child get free school meals if I receive Universal Credit?
evidence: free school meals if you get any of the following
reference_answer: Yes, if your household income is £7,400 a year or less (after tax, not counting benefits). From the 2026 to 2027 school year, any family on Universal Credit qualifies, whatever the income.

question_en: Is school transport free if the school is far from home?
evidence: more than 2 miles away and the child is under 8
reference_answer: Yes, if it is the nearest suitable school and it is more than 2 miles away (child under 8) or more than 3 miles away (child 8 or over), or there is no safe walking route, or the child cannot walk because of SEND or a mobility problem.

question_en: At what age can my child leave school?
evidence: 16 by the end of the summer holidays
reference_answer: On the last Friday in June if they will be 16 by the end of the summer holidays. Until 18 they must stay in education, start an apprenticeship, or work or volunteer 20 hours a week with part-time education or training.

question_en: What support can my child get for special educational needs?
evidence: SEN support - support given in school
reference_answer: SEN support in school (for example speech therapy), or an education, health and care (EHC) plan for more complex needs, up to age 25. Talk to the school's SENCO.

question_en: How do I complain about my child's state school?
evidence: different ways to complain in England
reference_answer: Talk to the school first. If that does not solve it, use the school's formal complaints procedure; after that you can complain to the Department for Education or Ofsted.

question_en: Can my landlord evict me without giving a reason?
evidence: section 21 process
reference_answer: No. From 1 May 2026 the 'no fault' section 21 process ended. The landlord must give a legal reason (a ground for possession) and the correct notice, usually 4 months.

question_en: How often can my landlord increase the rent?
evidence: increase the rent once a year
reference_answer: Once a year, and not in the first 12 months of a new tenancy. The landlord must use Form 4A and give at least 2 months' notice. You can challenge an increase above market rent.

question_en: My landlord took a deposit from me. Does it have to be protected?
evidence: Deposit Protection Service
reference_answer: Yes, if you have an assured periodic tenancy and the deposit was taken on or after 6 April 2007. It must go into a government-approved scheme within 30 days.

question_en: How can I get help paying my rent if I am on a low income?
evidence: help you pay your rent
reference_answer: Housing Benefit can help pay rent if you are unemployed, on a low income or claiming benefits, but new claims are only possible at State Pension age or in supported, sheltered or temporary housing. Most people claim Universal Credit instead.

question_en: How do I apply for council housing?
evidence: join a waiting list
reference_answer: Apply through your local council. You usually join a waiting list, and councils decide who gets housing using points or bands based on need.

question_en: I am about to lose my home. Can the council help me?
evidence: homeless or about to lose your home
reference_answer: Yes. Contact the local council for help and advice if you are homeless or about to lose your home.

question_en: Does my landlord have to keep my rented home in good repair?
evidence: safe and in a good state of repair
reference_answer: Yes. The landlord must keep the property safe and in a good state of repair, and is always responsible for the structure, heating, hot water, gas, wiring and sanitary fittings.

question_en: How much notice must my landlord give before visiting the property?
evidence: 24 hours
reference_answer: At least 24 hours' notice, at a reasonable time of day, unless it is an emergency.

question_en: Do I get a council tax discount if I live alone?
evidence: 25% off your bill
reference_answer: Yes, 25% off the bill if you live on your own. You need to apply.

question_en: What can I do if my council or housing association wants to evict me?
evidence: stop or delay the eviction
reference_answer: You may be able to stop or delay it. Get advice from Citizens Advice or Shelter and check if you can get legal aid. The landlord must give written notice and needs a court order.

question_en: How do I register with a GP surgery?
evidence: change your current GP surgery online
reference_answer: Online through the NHS website (or the NHS App to change surgery), or with a paper form or the surgery's own website. It is free.

question_en: Do I need proof of address or immigration status to register with a GP?
evidence: do not need ID, proof of address
reference_answer: No. You only need basic information such as your name, date of birth and address. You do not need ID, proof of address or proof of immigration status.

question_en: When should I use NHS 111?
evidence: if you think you need medical help right now
reference_answer: When you think you need medical help right now but it is not life-threatening, or you are not sure where to go. Use 111 online (age 5 and over) or call 111.

question_en: When should I go to A&E?
evidence: serious injuries and life-threatening emergencies
reference_answer: For serious injuries and life-threatening emergencies.

question_en: When should I call 999?
evidence: 999 is for life-threatening emergencies
reference_answer: For life-threatening emergencies, such as serious road accidents, strokes and heart attacks.

question_en: How can I find an NHS dentist?
evidence: Ask for an NHS appointment
reference_answer: Contact any NHS dentist and ask for an NHS appointment. If you cannot find one, contact your local integrated care board (ICB).

question_en: How much does a basic NHS dental check-up cost?
reference_answer: A Band 1 check-up (examination, X-rays if needed, scaling) costs £27.90.

question_en: Can a pharmacy give me prescription medicine without seeing a GP?
evidence: This is called Pharmacy First
reference_answer: Yes, through Pharmacy First, for some conditions such as sore throat, earache, sinusitis, impetigo, infected insect bites, UTIs and shingles (age limits apply).

question_en: Can I get help with health costs if I have a low income?
evidence: HC2 certificate
reference_answer: Yes, through the NHS Low Income Scheme if your savings are under £16,000 (£23,250 in a care home). It gives full help (HC2) or partial help (HC3).

question_en: How much is the immigration health surcharge for students?
evidence: £776 per year for students
reference_answer: £776 per year for students and their dependants.

At what age does my child start school?
evidence: start reception full-time in september after their fourth birthday
reference_answer: Most children start reception full-time in the September after their fourth birthday.

question_en: How many children can be in an infant class?
evidence: class size is limited to 30
reference_answer: In reception, year 1 and year 2 classes are limited to 30 children.

question_en: What happens if my child does not get a place at any school I applied for?
evidence: the local council must provide a place at another school
reference_answer: Yes. If your child is not offered any of the schools you applied for, the council must provide a place at another school, usually the nearest one with places.

question_en: How long does a school have to keep its waiting list open?
evidence: for at least the first term of each school year
reference_answer: The admission authority must keep a waiting list open for at least the first term of each school year.

question_en: What happens if I do not pay a school absence fine?
evidence: if you do not pay the fine in 28 days
reference_answer: If you do not pay the fine in 28 days you may be taken to court, where you could be fined up to £2,500, get a community order or a jail sentence of up to 3 months.

question_en: When is my child allowed to miss school?
evidence: you have advance permission from the school
reference_answer: Only if they are too ill to go in, or you have advance permission from the school.

question_en: Can my child in reception get free school meals?
evidence: reception class year 1 year 2
reference_answer: Yes. Children in reception, year 1 and year 2 at a government-funded school can get free school meals.

question_en: My child is 9. How far away must the school be to get free school transport?
evidence: more than 3 miles away and the child is 8 or over
reference_answer: For a child aged 8 or over, free transport applies if the nearest suitable school is more than 3 miles away (other conditions can also qualify).

question_en: How many branded uniform items can a school make me buy?
evidence: more than 3 items of branded school uniform
reference_answer: From September 2026 schools should not require more than 3 branded items (4 for secondary and middle schools if one is a tie).

question_en: How long does the council take to decide on an EHC plan?
evidence: within 16 weeks
reference_answer: The local authority must tell you within 16 weeks whether an EHC plan will be made; the final plan is due within 20 weeks of the request.

question_en: Can I ask the council to assess my child for an EHC plan?
evidence: you can ask your local authority to carry out an assessment
reference_answer: Yes. You can ask your local authority to carry out an EHC needs assessment.

question_en: What is a free school?
evidence: free schools are funded by the government but are not run by the local authority
reference_answer: Free schools are funded by the government but not run by the local authority. They are all-ability, can change term lengths and do not have to follow the national curriculum.

question_en: Do academies charge school fees?
evidence: academies do not charge fees
reference_answer: No. Academies are funded directly by the government and do not charge fees.

question_en: Where can I find my child's school holiday dates?
evidence: holiday dates on your local council
reference_answer: Term, half term and holiday dates are on your local council's website.

question_en: My child left school at 16. What must they do until they are 18?
evidence: stay in full-time education, for example at a college
reference_answer: Until 18 they must stay in full-time education, start an apprenticeship, or spend 20 hours or more a week working or volunteering while in part-time education or training.

question_en: How long do I have to complain to the SEND tribunal about disability discrimination at school?
evidence: within 6 months of the discrimination taking place
reference_answer: You must send a disability discrimination complaint to the SEND tribunal within 6 months of the discrimination. It is free.

question_en: What is the most a landlord can ask for as a deposit?
evidence: rent for the year is less than £50,000
reference_answer: Up to 5 weeks' rent if the yearly rent is under £50,000, or 6 weeks' rent if it is £50,000 or more. A holding deposit can be up to one week's rent.

question_en: How quickly must my landlord put my deposit in a protection scheme?
evidence: within 30 days of getting it
reference_answer: Your landlord or letting agent must put the deposit in a government-approved scheme within 30 days of getting it.

question_en: How long does my landlord have to give my deposit back when I move out?
evidence: within 10 days of you both agreeing
reference_answer: The landlord must return the deposit within 10 days of you both agreeing how much you will get back.

question_en: How much notice do I need to give to leave my rented home?
evidence: end it by giving 2 months
reference_answer: You can end an assured periodic tenancy by giving 2 months' notice in writing, and you keep paying rent during the notice period.

question_en: How much rent can a landlord ask me to pay in advance?
evidence: a maximum of 1 month
reference_answer: Nothing before you sign the tenancy agreement; after signing, a maximum of 1 month's rent in advance.

question_en: Can I keep a pet in my rented home?
evidence: you can ask to keep a pet in the property
reference_answer: Yes, you can ask. The landlord must consider the request and should give a reason if they refuse.

question_en: Can a landlord refuse to rent to me because I get benefits?
evidence: cannot refuse to rent a property to a tenant who is on benefits
reference_answer: No. A landlord cannot refuse to rent to a tenant because they are on benefits or have children.

question_en: My landlord will not do the repairs. Who can help me?
evidence: environmental health department at your local council
reference_answer: Contact the environmental health department at your local council. It must act if the problems could harm you.

question_en: Does my landlord have to do a gas safety check?
evidence: annual gas safety check
reference_answer: Yes. A registered engineer must do an annual gas safety check, and the landlord must give you a copy before you move in or within 28 days of the check.

question_en: How much can a landlord be fined for illegally evicting a tenant?
evidence: fine of up to £40,000
reference_answer: Local councils can prosecute landlords or give a fine of up to £40,000 for harassment or illegal eviction.

question_en: What counts as harassment by a landlord?
evidence: withholding keys
reference_answer: Harassment can include stopping services like electricity, withholding keys, refusing repairs, threats, threatening to change the locks and opening or taking post.

question_en: Will my Housing Benefit go down if I have a spare bedroom?
evidence: reduced by 14%
reference_answer: In council or social housing, Housing Benefit is reduced by 14% of the eligible rent for 1 spare bedroom and 25% for 2 or more.

question_en: How long does it take to get the first Universal Credit payment?
evidence: around 5 weeks to get your first payment
reference_answer: It usually takes around 5 weeks. You can apply for an advance if you need money while you wait.

question_en: How much savings can I have and still claim Universal Credit?
evidence: £16,000 or less in money, savings and investments
reference_answer: You must have £16,000 or less in money, savings and investments. Over £6,000 reduces the payment.

question_en: How much extra Universal Credit do I get for each child?
evidence: £303.94 a month for each child
reference_answer: £303.94 a month for each child who lives with you, with an extra £47.94 for a first child born before 6 April 2017.

question_en: Do students have to pay Council Tax?
evidence: a full-time student do not have to pay council tax
reference_answer: Households where everyone is a full-time student do not have to pay Council Tax. If you get a bill, apply for an exemption.

question_en: I am struggling to pay my Council Tax. Can I pay it over 12 months?
evidence: over 12 months instead of 10
reference_answer: Yes. Contact your council straight away; it can spread payments over 12 months instead of 10.

question_en: How long does it take to be registered with a GP after I apply online?
evidence: usually be within 5 days
reference_answer: You should be told when you are registered, usually within 5 days of the surgery getting your details, but it may take longer.

question_en: Can I see a GP if I am only staying in an area for a few weeks?
evidence: temporary patient for up to 3 months
reference_answer: Yes. You can register with a GP surgery as a temporary patient for up to 3 months using a temporary services form.

question_en: If a GP surgery refuses to register me, do they have to tell me why?
evidence: write to you within 14 days to explain why
reference_answer: Yes. If a GP surgery refuses to register you, it must write to you within 14 days to explain why.

question_en: Can I get a GP appointment in the evening or at the weekend?
evidence: saturdays between 9am and 5pm
reference_answer: Yes. You can see a healthcare professional on weekday evenings 6.30pm to 8pm and on Saturdays 9am to 5pm.

question_en: Can I use 111 online for my 3-year-old?
evidence: 111 online is for people aged 5 and over
reference_answer: No. 111 online is for people aged 5 and over; call 111 for a child under 5.

question_en: I have run out of my regular medicine. Can 111 help?
evidence: emergency supply of regularly prescribed medicine
reference_answer: Yes. 111 online can send a request to a local pharmacy for an emergency supply of your regular medicine until you can get your repeat prescription.

question_en: Should I drive myself to A&E?
evidence: do not drive to a&e
reference_answer: No. Do not drive to A&E. Ask someone to drive you or call 999 for an ambulance.

question_en: If I call 999, will an ambulance always come?
evidence: calling 999 does not always mean an ambulance will be sent
reference_answer: No. Calling 999 does not always mean an ambulance is sent; you may be told to make your own way to A&E or be seen elsewhere.

question_en: Do I have to pay again if I need more dental treatment a few weeks later?
evidence: within 2 months, you do not have to pay extra
reference_answer: If the further treatment within 2 months is in the same or a lower band, you do not pay extra; a higher band means paying the higher fee.

question_en: Do I have to pay to get my dentures repaired on the NHS?
evidence: your false teeth (dentures) need to be repaired
reference_answer: No, repairing dentures is free. If they cannot be repaired, you pay for new ones.

question_en: What should I do with old medicines I no longer need?
evidence: take it to your pharmacy to be disposed of safely
reference_answer: Do not put it in the bin or flush it away. Take it to a pharmacy to be disposed of safely.

question_en: Can I get free prescriptions while I am pregnant?
evidence: maternity exemption (matex) certificate
reference_answer: Yes. Ask your midwife or GP about the maternity exemption (MATEX) certificate, which gives free NHS prescriptions and free dental care.

question_en: What is the savings limit for the NHS Low Income Scheme?
evidence: £16,000 for everyone else
reference_answer: Your savings, investments or property (not your home) must not be over £16,000, or £23,250 if you live permanently in a care home.

question_en: How do I apply for the NHS Low Income Scheme by post?
evidence: complete an hc1 form
reference_answer: Apply online, or by post using an HC1 form sent to the address on the form.

question_en: I am visiting England. Is A&E free for me?
evidence: are exempt from charges
reference_answer: Yes. A&E services are free to everyone, but emergency treatment after being admitted to hospital is not included.

question_en: How much do overseas visitors pay for NHS hospital treatment?
evidence: charged at 150% of the national nhs rate
reference_answer: If you are not ordinarily resident and must pay for NHS hospital treatment, you are charged 150% of the national NHS rate.

question_en: When should I have the whooping cough vaccine in pregnancy?
evidence: around 20 weeks pregnant
reference_answer: The whooping cough (pertussis) vaccine is offered around 20 weeks of pregnancy.
